newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton ends barely down ahead of USDA data.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton ends barely down ahead of USDA data.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures settled tightly mixed in cautious trade ahead of Thursday's report on exports and new sales, trading sources said.
They expect the U.S. Department of Agricutlure report to show new sales between 50,000 and 70,000 bales in both the old and new crops.
"I have a feeling the numbers will be friendly, which may help to rally the market," a dealers said.
Earlier in the week, the USDA pegged exports at 7.3 million 480-lb bales for the 1997/98 crop. Exports for the current crop are expected to reach 7.0 million bales.
The most-active July contract ended 0.03 cent weaker at 72.30 cents per lb, after trading in a narrow range between 72.40 to 72.05 cents. New-crop December finished 0.13 cent firmer at 74.61 cents.
Trade was estimated at a light 4,000 lots compared with Tuesday's official 4,431 lots.
Early speculative selling between 72.10 and 72.15 cents in July caused the market to weaken early, but scale-down buying by the trade held July over its downside target of 72.00 cents, dealers said.
They said a move below support could trigger stops and pressure the contract to its lifetime low of 71.00 cents.
"But it seems to be holding, which is somewhat important technically," a traders said, adding that buy stops were triggered at 72.00 and 72.00 cents in Monday's rally.
"So long as we hold we'll probably work higher," he said.
Resistance in July was cited at 73.00 cents.
